---
title: "Build spatiotemporal flowering maps"
---

## Example: _Cercis canadensis_

Here is an example of combining the spatial prediction from _deepbiosphere_ with the phenological prediction from the finite mixture models.

### Deepbiosphere prediction
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: false
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(tidyterra)
library(sf)
library(terra)
source("R/mix_mods.R")

padf <- rast("data-raw/big/pa_2017_merge_block_mosaic.tif")

# Cercis canadensis
ccdf <- padf[["Cercis canadensis"]]

ggplot() + geom_spatraster(data=ccdf) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "rocket",
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Deepbiosphere prediction of Cercis canadensis",
    fill = ""
  )

```

### Phenology curve (thinned)

Comparing the finite mixture model distributions to the flowering records distribution, I can guess that the first distribution (`dist = 1`) corresponds with flowering.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

cc <- readRDS("data/top100_gdd_thin.rds") |> filter(species == "Cercis canadensis")
cc.mix <- readRDS("data/results/mixmods_flr100_thin.rds")[["Cercis canadensis"]]

cc.dist <- make_dist_mix(cc.mix, 50)

ggplot(cc, aes(gdd)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 50, fill = "yellowgreen") +
  geom_histogram(data = cc %>% dplyr::filter(flowering),
                 binwidth = 50, fill = "tan1") +
  labs(x=NULL, y="Count") +
  geom_line(data = cc.dist,
            mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, color = dist)) +
  geom_text(
    data = cc |> summarize(Freq = n()),
    mapping = aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = Freq),
    hjust   = 1.1,
    vjust   = 1.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red3","turquoise4","burlywood4"))+
  egg::theme_article() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,4000))


# ggsave("plots/C_canadensis_mixmod.png",bg="white",height=3,width=6)

```

### Apply estimated bloom curve 

Use the matching finite mixture model curve for _Cercis canadensis_ bloom reports to predict bloom probability from growing degree days

```{r}
#| eval: false

# use distribution 1
cc.d <- 1

cc.mu <- cc.mix$mu[cc.d]
cc.sigma <- cc.mix$sigma[cc.d]

pa_gdd <- rast("data-raw/big/pa_gdd2017_256m.tif")

# apply pnorm function to stack of gdd rasters
cc_gdd_cdf <- terra::app(pa_gdd, pnorm, mean = cc.mu, sd = cc.sigma)

# add a 0 raster at the beginning of the gdd time series to substract from
cc_gdd_0 <- pa_gdd[[1]]*0
cc_gdd_0cdf <- c(cc_gdd_0, cc_gdd_cdf)

# find difference in cumulative probability between weeks
cc_flrpb <- terra::diff(cc_gdd_0cdf, filename = "data-raw/big/flrpb_Ccanadensis.tif")

```

![Animation of _Cercis canadensis_ bloom probability in PA](plots/flrpb_Ccanadensis.gif)

### _C. canadensis_ bloom probability in space and time

Multiply species distribution from _deepbiosphere_ with gdd-based bloom probability from finite mixture model to estimate overall probability of bloom occurence in space and time.

```{r}
#| eval: false

# load deepbiosphere raster
padf <- rast("data-raw/big/pa_2017_merge_block_mosaic.tif")

# Cercis canadensis
ccdf <- padf[["Cercis canadensis"]]

cc_stbp <- cc_flrpb * ccdf

```

![Animation of _C. canadensis_ spatiotemporal bloom occurence probability](plots/stflrpb_Ccanadensis.gif)
